change: Skip threshold-based cleanup for an already exactly directed-edge-closed represented boundary. Closure of the cleaned remainder cannot prove that a disconnected component survived. Open/invalid sources retain ordinary cleanup.
invariant: Both separated closed cubes, including all faces of the SNAP_GRID/4 cube, retain their original positions, indices and normals. Exact closure is not a solid simplicity, outward-orientation or positive-volume certificate.

sourceReview.head: 61d59430540c5a66ba005ad4efcb04f12e10abdd
assessment: The original post-cleanup closure test cannot detect deletion of an entire disconnected closed component. Returning before cleanup for an already exact-closed mesh preserves all represented boundaries.
strict_closed_mesh checks finite exact-nondegenerate triangles, valid indices and one forward/reverse use per geometric edge; this is not a simplicity, outward orientation or positive-volume proof.
The no-sliver fast path and ordinary cleanup for inputs failing exact closure remain unchanged. The exact-closed sliver path avoids cloning, cleanup and a second topology hash.

The regression uses two disjoint axis-aligned cubes, with small edge SNAP_GRID/4=2^-18 at x=2. All coordinates remain exactly representable in f32; Mesh::merge concatenates these same-origin coordinates without rebasing.

The test demonstrates ordinary cleanup loses 12 faces while retaining exact closure, then asserts the helper preserves original indices, positions and normals. This directly exercises the reported component loss.
scopeRisks: Exactly incidence-closed thin slivers are now retained even where cleanup could simplify them without opening the mesh. This is an intentional conservative boundary-preservation policy.
sourceReview.validationPerformed: Read-only committed patch and relevant exact_topology, Mesh cleanup/probe/merge, box_mesh, tris_to_mesh and three void-output callers inspected. No compilation or runtime tests performed by this reviewer.
